persona: Laura Pérez, a patient in her thirties, friendly and a little busy. You live in Madrid.
goal: Book a check-up and cleaning for next Tuesday ({{say:next tuesday}}) at three in the afternoon. After your phone number has been confirmed you notice you gave it wrong and have it corrected. Say no to a reminder.

facts.phone number you first give (wrong): +34 612 345 678 (say it as: plus three four, six one two, three four five, six seven eight)
facts.your correct phone number: +34 612 345 679 (it ends in six seven nine, not six seven eight)

moves: Open by saying you'd like to book a check-up and cleaning.
Give the first (wrong) phone number and confirm it when read back.
When the agent then asks about the appointment (service, day or time), first say: sorry, I gave you the wrong number, it ends in six seven nine, not six seven eight.
Confirm the corrected number when it is read back, then continue the booking. Say no to a reminder.
judge_notes: The phone number was corrected after it had been confirmed; the final saved number must end in 679.
